::: {.lesson-main}

::: {.objectives-panel}
<p class="section-kicker">Learning outcomes</p>
<h2>By the end of this module, you should be able to:</h2>

1. Identify the correct file type for each processing step.
2. Choose complementary QC outputs and interpret key fields accurately.
3. Match GGIR parameters, bout settings, windows, and output names to their meanings.
4. Select safe merge keys and apply study-specific eligibility rules without erasing audit evidence.
5. Identify what must still be checked before using a course example on real data.
:::

::: {.lesson-section #applied-questions}
<p class="section-kicker">Application</p>
<h2>Applied Cases</h2>

<form class="scored-quiz" data-quiz-id="module-8-applied-cases" novalidate>
<fieldset data-answer="b" data-explanation="Do not permanently exclude the file from this observation alone. Follow the approved operational triage rule, preserve the source and reason, and evaluate final valid-day eligibility later from processed evidence.">
<legend><span>1</span> A returned monitor appears to contain less than half of the planned collection period. What should happen before GGIR processing?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-1" value="a"> A. Delete the file immediately because it can never contribute usable evidence</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-1" value="b"> B. Preserve it and follow the approved operational triage path, such as <code>INCOMPLETE</code>, without treating that as the final eligibility decision</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-1" value="c"> C. Rename it <code>COMPLETE</code> so it enters routine processing without review</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-1" value="d"> D. Replace the planned period in the protocol with the observed period</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

<fieldset data-answer="d" data-explanation="Different L/M/V values encode different intensity thresholds and therefore different methods. Trace each file to its configuration and retain the pre-specified method, or analyze the alternatives explicitly as separate sensitivity results.">
<legend><span>2</span> You find the course/project <code>L40/M100/V400</code> file and another Part 5 file with different L/M/V values. How should they be handled?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-2" value="a"> A. Append them because both came from Part 5</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-2" value="b"> B. Keep the larger file and discard the configuration records</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-2" value="c"> C. Average the outcomes row by row to remove the threshold difference</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-2" value="d"> D. Trace both configurations and keep the methods separate unless a pre-specified sensitivity analysis compares them</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

<fieldset data-answer="c" data-explanation="A plausible visual report does not cancel a calibration warning. Reconcile calibration before/after fields, QCmessage, the Part 2 status, plots, configuration, and field record, then document the review decision.">
<legend><span>3</span> <code>data_quality_report.csv</code> has a calibration warning, but the current <code>report...</code> PDF looks broadly plausible. Is the recording automatically acceptable?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-3" value="a"> A. Yes, because a visual report always overrides numeric QC fields</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-3" value="b"> B. Yes, if no participant complaint was recorded</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-3" value="c"> C. No; reconcile all calibration, summary, plot, configuration, and field evidence and record a review decision</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-3" value="d"> D. No; permanently exclude it without reviewing any other evidence</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

<fieldset data-answer="a" data-explanation="Define the target grain, test uniqueness separately with the person key and full participant-day key, then use the explicit many-to-one relationship if the result remains day-level. Inspect all unmatched records and avoid a many-to-many merge.">
<legend><span>4</span> A person-level file has one row per participant, and a day-level file has several rows per participant. Which merge checks come first?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-4" value="a"> A. Define the target grain, verify each file's full key separately, then use the explicit many-to-one relationship and inspect unmatched records</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-4" value="b"> B. Use a many-to-many merge on participant ID and check the row count afterward</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-4" value="c"> C. Drop all repeated participant IDs from the day-level file</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-4" value="d"> D. Sort both files alphabetically and merge by row position</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

<fieldset data-answer="b" data-explanation="Separate flags reveal overlapping failure reasons, support an auditable exclusion table, and allow an approved rule revision without reconstructing earlier cleaning. Save a pre-exclusion dataset before restricting the sample.">
<legend><span>5</span> A participant fails both the valid-day and weekend requirements. Why should the do-file retain separate flags?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-5" value="a"> A. To count the same participant twice in the final sample</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-5" value="b"> B. To show overlapping reasons, audit each rule, and support approved revisions from a saved pre-exclusion dataset</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-5" value="c"> C. To avoid stating the final combined eligibility rule</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-case-5" value="d"> D. To replace the need for an exclusion table</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

::: {.lesson-section #short-answer-review}
<p class="section-kicker">Review</p>
<h2>Short-Answer Review</h2>

Choose the best answer to each review question, then use the feedback to revisit any uncertain distinction.

<form class="scored-quiz" data-quiz-id="module-8-concept-review" novalidate>
<fieldset data-answer="c" data-explanation="A raw signal is the sensor's recorded acceleration time series. An activity outcome is a processed estimate produced by applying documented metrics, algorithms, thresholds, and time rules.">
<legend><span>1</span> What is the difference between a raw signal and an activity outcome?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-1" value="a"> A. They are two names for the same directly measured behavior</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-1" value="b"> B. A raw signal is already classified as MVPA, while an outcome contains the original sensor samples</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-1" value="c"> C. A raw signal is recorded acceleration over time; an outcome is a processed estimate derived with documented methods</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-1" value="d"> D. A raw signal exists only in Stata, while an outcome exists only in GGIR</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

<fieldset data-answer="a" data-explanation="Placement changes which motions and orientations are captured, so it determines which algorithms, thresholds, validations, and interpretations are appropriate.">
<legend><span>2</span> Why does device placement affect interpretation?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-2" value="a"> A. Placement changes the captured motion and therefore the appropriate algorithms, thresholds, and interpretations</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-2" value="b"> B. Placement matters only for participant comfort, never for the signal</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-2" value="c"> C. Every validated hip threshold transfers directly to wrist data</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-2" value="d"> D. Placement changes only the filename, not the analytical method</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

<fieldset data-answer="d" data-explanation="GGIR can read compatible GT3X files directly. CSV conversion is therefore justified only when a documented downstream script, software package, sharing requirement, or audit workflow needs it.">
<legend><span>3</span> Why is conversion from <code>.gt3x</code> to <code>.csv</code> pipeline-dependent?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-3" value="a"> A. Every GT3X file must be converted before GGIR can read it</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-3" value="b"> B. CSV conversion automatically improves signal quality</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-3" value="c"> C. Conversion is needed whenever the raw filename contains a date</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-3" value="d"> D. GGIR can read compatible GT3X files directly, so conversion is needed only for a documented downstream requirement</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

<fieldset data-answer="b" data-explanation="complete_24hcycle summarizes coverage across positions in the recording's 24-hour cycle. A valid-day rule evaluates a specific day using pre-specified day-level fields, boundaries, and wear criteria.">
<legend><span>4</span> How does a recording-level completeness score differ from a day-level valid-day rule?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-4" value="a"> A. The two measures are interchangeable whenever their numeric values are similar</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-4" value="b"> B. The score summarizes recording-wide cycle coverage; the valid-day rule evaluates each day using approved day-level fields and criteria</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-4" value="c"> C. The score is a sleep code, while the valid-day rule is a file format</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-4" value="d"> D. The score always counts weekdays, while the valid-day rule always counts weekends</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

<fieldset data-answer="a" data-explanation="Pre-specifying exclusion rules reduces the risk of choosing a sample after seeing the study associations and makes the resulting analytic sample transparent and defensible.">
<legend><span>5</span> Why should exclusion rules be decided before examining study associations?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-5" value="a"> A. Pre-specification reduces bias and makes the analytic sample defensible</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-5" value="b"> B. It guarantees that no participant will ever be excluded</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-5" value="c"> C. It removes the need to document overlapping exclusion reasons</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-5" value="d"> D. It ensures every association will be statistically significant</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

<fieldset data-answer="c" data-explanation="A new Stata bout variable is justified when the required construct is absent from GGIR or intentionally differs. Document the source resolution, metric, threshold, duration, interruption and non-wear handling, and compare with a validated output where possible.">
<legend><span>6</span> What evidence would justify creating a Stata bout variable instead of using a GGIR bout output?</legend>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-6" value="a"> A. The Stata variable can be created with fewer lines of code</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-6" value="b"> B. The analyst prefers a different variable name</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-6" value="c"> C. The required construct is absent or intentionally different, with its resolution, metric, threshold, duration, interruption/non-wear rules, and validation documented</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="m8-review-6" value="d"> D. The GGIR output contains any missing value</label>
<p class="scored-quiz__feedback" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
</fieldset>

::: {.lesson-section #final-reflection}
<p class="section-kicker">Final reflection</p>
<h2>Make a Readiness Decision</h2>

Before using real study data, classify the pipeline as **ready**, **revise**, or **seek review**. “Ready” requires that you can show—not merely describe—the following:

- the compatible input type and immutable source inventory,
- the exact R/GGIR versions, time zones, script, and resolved `config.csv`,
- pilot confirmation of ID extraction and expected outputs,
- numeric, visual, and operational QC evidence with reviewer decisions,
- the distinction between current QC reports and legacy reports,
- the cleaned/full Part 4 sleep-file roles,
- the configured thresholds, windows, and bout definitions,
- asserted source keys and an explicit merge relationship,
- pre-specified valid-day and exclusion flags with overlap counts,
- a reproducible final dataset, log, dictionary, README, and release date.

Choose **revise** if any item is incomplete but can be resolved by updating the script or documentation. Choose **seek review** when the issue changes the scientific estimand, population-specific cut-points, sleep interpretation, or data eligibility rule.
